Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS: 3019 ^1973 
3. JMaterial 

3.1 One-P/ece Construct/on — High speed steel. * 

3.2 Two-Piece Construction 

a) Cutting Portion — High speed steel. 

b) Shank Portion —Carbon steel with tensile strength not less than 700 MPa [1l\/IPa = 0*1 kgf/ 

mm2 ( approx ) ]. To meet this rec^ulrement, the hardness value shall not 
be less than 185 f/B measured at one third length away from the rear end 
of the tool. 

Note — Unless otherwise speciFfed#ie high speed steel shall be according to T83W6Mo5Cr4V2 or T72W18Cr4V1 
according to 13:7291-1974 'Specification for high speed tool steels' or equivalent in which case major constituents 
shall be specified by the manufacturer, 

4. Hardness — 750 H/ to 830 W ( 62 H/?C to 65 HRC) [seelS : 1501 - 1968 Method for Vickers 
hardness test for steel ( first revision ) and IS ; 1586 - 1968 Method for Rockwell hardness test ( B and 
C scales ) for steel ( first revision )]. 

4.1 For two-piece construction, the hardness shall be maintained over the length /g. 

5. General Requirements 

5.1 The shank sections and designations of tool shanks shall be according to IS : 1983-1962 
' Specification for shank sections for single point turning and planing tools '. 

5.2 The figures are indicative of dimensions only and do not specify design features. 

6. Workmanship and Finish — The tools shall be soundly forged to shape and shall be free from 
burrs, rust, seams, cracks or other manufacturing defects. The butt-welding in case of tools of two- 
piece, construction shall be sound. The tools shall be supplied well-finished, with the cutting edges 
and relief angles ground and ready for use. 

7. Marking — To be marked on the rear left-hand side of shank with designation of shank, hand of 
cutting ( R or L ) and the manufacturer's name or trade-mark. 

7.1 Certificat/on Marking — DetaWs available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

8. Protective Coating* and Packing — The tools shall be painted for rust -proofing. The cutting 
portion of all tools shall be protected against damage by a suitable plastic coating. The tools shall 
then be packed in boxes or containers for safe handling. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1965 on the basis of relevant DIN Standards. In the 
present revision tool section have been further rationalized and overall lengths have been reduced. The 
nose radii have been changed to conform to the work being done by ISO/TC 29 Small Toots. 

12 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
